clue.text: Check to do with one's skin

parts.note: re means concerning or to do with, as in a business letter
in the buff means naked, wearing only one's skin

explanation.surface: Someone examines a matter relating to their own complexion.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuff is a sharp refusal that halts someone, so a check in the sense of a setback or snub.

clue.text: Prepared to create a scene

parts.note: creating a scene sounds like making a fuss, but actors practise a stage scene before performing it

explanation.surface: Someone ready to make a public fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors practise lines and moves before a performance, so a practised scene is ready for staging.

clue.text: Capital investment for a man of the church

definitions.text: Capital investment for a man of the church

parts.words: Capital investment for a man of the church
parts.note: capital investment sounds financial, but read as head covering it means a cap invested on a priest's head

explanation.surface: A cleric putting money into a business.
explanation.definitionFit: A square cap worn by Roman Catholic clergy is a head garment for a priest.

clue.text: The good earth — where people enjoy rides

parts.note: fair means good or reasonable
ground is earth or soil

explanation.surface: A reverent phrase about fertile soil, followed by a funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: A site with roundabouts, big wheels and other amusements is where people go on rides.

clue.text: Kicking off and making a sudden movement

explanation.surface: A footballer starts the match with a jerky lurch.
explanation.definitionFit: Kicking off means beginning a game, and a sudden involuntary jump of surprise is also this word.

clue.text: Delight in one's car?

explanation.surface: Someone takes great pleasure in their motor.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapture or ecstasy is one sense; a vehicle as a means of travel is the other.

clue.text: Went on the right lines

parts.note: an ode is a poem, lines of verse

explanation.surface: Someone followed the correct track, perhaps on a train.
explanation.definitionFit: Rode means travelled on horseback or in a vehicle, that is, went.

clue.text: Cook can idle in this country

indicators.note: cooking the books means falsifying, so the letters are doctored into a new order

explanation.surface: A chef can lounge around in a certain nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceland is a nation in the North Atlantic.

clue.text: A way to occupy a fellow given to sudden outbursts

indicators.note: one piece moves in and occupies the other

parts.note: a guy is a fellow
St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A man with a fiery temper settling on a route.
explanation.definitionFit: Wind that blows in sudden bursts is gusty; figuratively, someone given to outbursts.

clue.text: Some of the best tunes deafen temporarily.

annotationWithheld.why: Some of the best tunes deafen temporarily (4): STUN is not a continuous run in 'best tunes' as printed (BESTTUNES has a doubled T); the setter's hidden word slip cannot be expressed by hid() over the printed words
annotationWithheld.clue: Some of the best tunes deafen temporarily.

clue.text: A player with pluck

parts.note: pluck reads as courage, but here it is the plucking of strings by a musician

explanation.surface: A brave sportsman or performer.
explanation.definitionFit: This musician plays a stringed instrument by plucking it rather than bowing.

clue.text: Speech can reveal where a person comes from

explanation.surface: Accent gives away someone's origins.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal talk to an audience is one sense; the street and house where one lives is the other.

clue.text: An opponent of stagnation making changes

indicators.note: the letters of stagnation are being altered, rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A reformer who opposes a static situation by bringing in change.
explanation.definitionFit: An adversary or rival is someone who opposes another, as in drama or argument.

clue.text: Not straight, so against entering means

indicators.note: one piece goes into another, entering it

parts.note: a way is a means or method
V is short for versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: A devious method of opposing something.
explanation.definitionFit: Undulating lines curve up and down rather than running in a line, like waved hair.

clue.text: Oriental coppers at one in speaking of a politician

parts.note: the sen is a small Japanese coin worth a hundredth of a yen
oral means spoken
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Asian police united in describing a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police, but means small coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Senatorial is the adjective for a senator, a member of a legislative upper house.

clue.text: Points to the left in Plymouth perhaps

parts.note: S and E are compass points, south and east
to as in so many to the pound means per, which is a
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Directions telling a sailor to steer left near a Devon harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' gives A in the sense of rate: ten to the pound is ten a pound. PLYMOUTH is a naval harbour town in Devon, south-west England; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Plymouth is one example of a harbour town on the coast where ships dock.

clue.text: Youngsters have seen great revolutions

indicators.note: the letters are turned over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Young people have witnessed great political upheavals.
explanation.definitionFit: Young people aged thirteen to nineteen are youngsters.

clue.text: Outstanding cricket expected

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket
due means expected, as a train is due

explanation.surface: A fine game of cricket that everyone was looking forward to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' looks like praise but means still unpaid or late.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill still unpaid, or anything late, is outstanding in the sense of not yet settled.

clue.text: Shift when fit

explanation.surface: Change when you're ready.
explanation.definitionFit: A makeshift means of coping is one sense; suitable or advantageous for a purpose is the other.

clue.text: Plea of French malefactor

parts.note: de is French for of
a fence is a criminal who receives stolen goods

explanation.surface: An appeal made by a French criminal in court.
explanation.definitionFit: In court, the accused's case in reply to a charge is their plea against it.

clue.text: Like a hundred in hand? Absolutely right!

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other

parts.note: a fist is a clenched hand
as means like
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A question about holding a century, then cheerful agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absolutely right!' sounds like agreement but means on the extreme political right.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of an authoritarian nationalist movement sit at the far end of the political right.

clue.text: The soap is free in this refreshment place

indicators.note: the letters of the words are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A café where the soap in the washroom costs nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A small café serving cups of tea and cakes is a refreshment place.

clue.text: Trial for man taking a piece of jewellery

parts.note: he refers to a man
a ring is a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: A man in court for stealing jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A judicial hearing is a trial of a case before a court.

clue.text: Ponder on the poet's inspiration

explanation.surface: Think about what gives a poet ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: To think over is one sense; the goddess believed to inspire writers is the other.

clue.text: Order up tea — or coffee

indicators.note: in a down light, up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A café choice between tea and coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine coffee, originally from Mocha in Yemen, also a coffee-chocolate drink.

clue.text: Such a contest will be closely fought

definitions.text: Such a contest will be closely fought

parts.words: Such a contest will be closely fought
parts.note: closely fought sounds like a tight game, but read literally it means fighters at arm's length

explanation.surface: A tight match with little between the sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat at close quarters, fists or blades against each other, is fought at very close range.

clue.text: Tie design

explanation.surface: A necktie's pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn game ends level, a tie; to sketch a plan is to design.

clue.text: Green cotton

explanation.surface: Fabric of a verdant colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A grassy area is a green; a fine linen or cotton fabric is the other sense.

clue.text: The small company in time makes money

parts.note: Co is the short form of company
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A small firm eventually becomes profitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Coins in circulation, the metal currency of a country, are its money.

clue.text: Russell would hold wrong-doing fashionable but stupid

indicators.note: one piece holds the others within it

parts.note: AE was the pen-name of the Irish poet George William Russell
sin is wrongdoing
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone named Russell thinks being naughty is trendy, which is silly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Irish writer George William Russell signed his work AE, a convention old crosswords used.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means donkey-like, hence foolish or senseless.

clue.text: Hosts in a drunken daze

indicators.note: drunken suggests reeling about, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Party hosts in an intoxicated stupor.
explanation.definitionFit: To daze someone is to stun or amaze them, as great surprise does.

clue.text: A hopeless situation, yet showing promise

explanation.surface: A desperate predicament that still holds hope.
explanation.definitionFit: A predicament or dire state is one sense; to pledge, as in pledging one's troth, is the other.
